title: Verification Document Access Flow
purpose: Document the flow for admin access to creator verification documents (ID and selfie) via Cloudflare R2 signed URLs with 60-second expiry
audience: Backend developers, security engineers, compliance officers, admin interface developers
description: When an admin requests a creator's verification documents, the admin controller calls admin.service.getVerificationDocs(userId), which queries the profiles table for the verification_data JSONB column containing idFilePath and selfieFilePath. The service validates that both file paths exist, then generates 60-second signed URLs from R2 for both files via StorageService.getPrivateSignedUrl(). The signed URLs are returned to the frontend and displayed in the VerificationDetailPanel component. Issues: ID documents contain PII (full name, DOB, address, ID number) transmitted via temporary URL; 60-second URLs expire quickly but are logged in browser history/network tab; there is no access audit recording who viewed whose verification docs and when.

preconditions: Admin has valid JWT and admin role (protectAndAdmin middleware)
Creator has submitted verification documents (verification_data has idFilePath and selfieFilePath)
R2 bucket podm-private exists and contains the referenced files
R2 S3 client is configured with valid credentials
postconditions: 60-second signed URLs for ID document and selfie returned to admin
URLs expire after 60 seconds — admin cannot refresh to re-view
No access audit record created — no log of who viewed whose docs or when
Browser network tab and history contain the signed URLs during the window

validationRules: Admin must have protectAndAdmin middleware (JWT + admin role)
userId must be a valid UUID of an existing user
verification_data must be non-null JSONB with idFilePath and selfieFilePath properties
File paths must reference existing R2 objects in podm-private/verification-docs/
businessRules: Signed URLs expire in 60 seconds from generation
No access audit — no record of who viewed verification docs or when
No user consent check — admin can view any user's verification docs
PII sensitivity: ID documents contain full name, DOB, address, and ID number
R2 object paths stored in verification_data are not user-accessible — admin only
securityConsiderations: 🔴 PII Sensitivity: ID documents contain full name, DOB, address, and ID number transmitted via temporary URL
🟡 60-second window: URLs expire quickly but are logged in browser history / network tab during validity
🔴 No Access Audit: no record of who viewed whose verification docs or when — GDPR compliance risk
R2 signed URLs use S3 SDK's getSignedUrl with 'getObject' operation — limited to read-only
URLs include R2 object key in path — reveals storage structure
No rate limiting on document access endpoint — admin could enumerate user verification status
performanceConsiderations: Two sequential R2 signed URL generation calls — adds ~100-300ms latency per call
StorageService has retry logic (3 attempts, exponential backoff) — adds latency on failure
No caching of signed URLs — each request generates new URLs (60-second expiry)
S3 SDK getSignedUrl is a local operation (no network call to R2) — fast, no API cost
